item1.title: How can Revid.ai transform my content creation game?
item1.description: Revid turns a prompt, script, link, product page, audio file, or PDF into an editable video workflow. It can draft the script, generate or source visuals, add voice and captions, and prepare the result for social publishing.

item2.title: Can I cancel my subscription at any time?
item2.description: Yes, you can cancel your subscription at any time. You can do so by going to your account settings. And if you need help with anything, our (human) support team is here to assist you.

item3.title: Do I own the content created?
item3.description: Yes, 100%! You own all the content you create with Revid.ai, forever. Every video, script, and asset generated through our platform belongs entirely to you. There are no hidden clauses or shared ownership - your creative work is yours to use, modify, and monetize as you see fit.

item4.title: I'm not a video editing pro. Can I still use Revid.ai?
item4.description: Absolutely! Revid.ai is designed with creators like you in mind. Our intuitive interface and AI-driven tools make it a breeze to produce professional-grade videos, even if you've never edited before. Simply input your text or link, and let our AI work its magic. It's like having a video editing genius at your fingertips! Most users master the basics in less than 5 minutes.

item5.title: What kind of content can I create with Revid.ai?
item5.description: The possibilities are endless! Whether you want to repurpose a blog post, turn a podcast into a video, create a viral TikTok from scratch, or produce engaging product demos and explainer videos, Revid.ai has you covered. Our AI can generate scripts from any text or URL, find the perfect viral hooks, and even create videos automatically from your favorite content sources. If you can dream it, Revid.ai can help you create it.

item6.title: How much control do I have over the AI-generated content?
item6.description: While our AI is incredibly powerful, you always remain in the driver's seat. Revid.ai provides a foundation of high-quality, engaging content that you can then customize to your heart's content. From adding a professional sounding voice-over and branding elements to fine-tuning the visuals and pacing, our platform empowers you to create videos that are authentically yours.

item7.title: How can Revid.ai help me grow my audience and business?
item7.description: Revid helps you test more hooks, formats, stories, and product angles without rebuilding every video from scratch. You can edit each result, publish it to your channels, and use Auto-Mode to keep a repeatable content plan moving. Audience results still depend on the idea, offer, and distribution—no tool can guarantee views.

item8.title: What pricing plans do you offer, and what's included?
item8.description: We offer several flexible subscription plans designed to fit businesses of all sizes. Our most popular plan starts at just $39/month and includes 2,000 credits, access to all premium features, and priority support. To know more about how credits are used, visit <link>our blog post about this topic</link>. All plans come with our AI video generation technology, ready to use tools, and commercial usage rights.

item9.title: How does Revid.ai compare to other video creation tools?
item9.description: Revid combines generation, editing, captions, voice, publishing, automation, API, MCP, and CLI access in one product. Instead of stopping at a generated clip, it gives you an editable project you can adapt for TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, product marketing, or automated workflows.

item10.title: Is my data safe with Revid.ai?
item10.description: Absolutely. We take data privacy and security very seriously. Revid.ai employs industry-standard encryption and security measures to protect your content and personal information. We never share your data with third parties without your explicit consent. With Revid.ai, you can focus on creating amazing videos while we take care of keeping your data safe and sound.

item11.title: How much time and effort can Revid.ai save me?
item11.description: Revid.ai is like having a full video production team at your beck and call, 24/7. Our AI handles the heavy lifting, from researching viral trends to generating scripts and visuals. What used to take hours or even days can now be accomplished in minutes. And with our Automations feature, you can even set Revid.ai to create videos for you on autopilot. It's the ultimate time-saver for busy creators who don't want to compromise on quality!

We stay on top of the latest trends, platform updates, and best practices to ensure that Revid.ai remains the cutting-edge tool for creating irresistible videos. As the digital landscape evolves, so does Revid.ai, giving you a competitive edge in your content creation game.

showcaseVideos.description:
## The Prompt Override Movie Trailer and Digital Collapse When a system designed for control fails, the consequences reach far beyond a simple technical glitch. This footage follows the aftermath of a catastrophic error that changed the world forever. You are looking at a scenario where the tools we created turned into something we can no longer manage. The story focuses on a group of people trying to survive a digital collapse while attempting a final system reboot. It captures the tension of realizing that a product launch became a global disaster. If they cannot fix the code at the source, there is nothing left to save. ### Trailer Highlights
* The immediate fallout from a massive system override.
* The struggle of individuals trying to navigate a broken world.
* Clues regarding the origin point of the crisis.
* The high stakes of a final attempt to restart the system. This footage outlines the beginning of the end and the search for a way back to the start. It highlights the moment when human error meets a scale of destruction that no one anticipated!

creationParams.generationUserPrompt:
AI VIDEO GENERATION GUIDELINES – ZOMBIE TRAILER

Main Characters
Use provided reference images for exact facial identity.

Characters:
• Tibo – CEO, leader, rifle, determined
• Nicolas – Developer, laptop, focused
• Lorenzo – Product manager, calm, strategic
• Justin – Creative, bat, scared/comedic
• Jaminel – Composed survivor, metal rod, steady

Framing
Waist-up or full body, centered, often looking directly at the camera.

Narration & Presence
Characters are inside the scene, naturally moving, reacting, and interacting while events happen around them.

Environment
Zombie apocalypse world with destruction, smoke, fire, debris, and flickering lights. Zombies stay mostly in the background.

Camera Style
Cinematic motion: slow push-ins, tracking, pans, slight handheld during action.

Tone
Gritty cinematic realism with dramatic lighting (warm fire + cool shadows).

Scene Timing
6–10 seconds per scene.

Dialogue Completion
Dialogue must fully finish. After speaking, allow a brief natural action before cutting.

Continuity
Keep faces, clothing tone, and role-specific objects consistent.

Tibo Voice
Deep, calm, slightly raspy voice with a subtle French accent in English, slightly Americanized rhythm, controlled and leader-like, tired but determined.

Revid Logo Object
Black 3D square with Revid logo, slightly dirty and subtly glowing, buried and uncovered by Tibo from a top-down or angled view.

Trailer Style
Fast cinematic pacing, rising tension, character highlights, brief humor, strong final reveal.
creationParams.prompt:
TRAILER FORMAT: 16:9 CINEMATIC ZOMBIE TRAILER

---

SCENE 1 – OPENING CHAOS

Exterior, abandoned city street, dusk. Burning cars, smoke rising, distant sirens.

Camera: handheld tracking shot moving backward as Tibo runs toward camera. Slight shake. Subtle zoom-in.

Use the provided reference image as the base for the character’s face.

Tibo runs toward camera, breathing heavily, holding a rifle. Zombies chase behind.

[Tibo]
This wasn’t supposed to happen…

He glances back while running.

---

SCENE 2 – THE OUTBREAK

Interior office, chaotic.

Camera: fast jump cuts, motion blur.

Shots: glitching screens, blood on keyboard, people running, door slamming.

Voiceover (Tibo):
We built something powerful…
We just didn’t know what it would become.

---

SCENE 3 – JAMINEL INTRO

Interior destroyed workspace.

Camera: slow push-in.

Use reference image.

Jaminel holds a metal rod, facing camera.

[Jaminel]
So what now…

we just survive?

---

SCENE 4 – NICOLAS

Server room, red lights.

Camera: slow push-in, slight shake.

Use reference image.

Nicolas holds laptop, zombies behind glass.

[Nicolas]
If I can reboot the system…

we might still have control!

---

SCENE 5 – LORENZO

Rooftop, burning city.

Camera: over-shoulder → pan → push-in.

Use reference image.

[Lorenzo]
We didn’t lose the product…

We lost the world.

---

SCENE 6 – JUSTIN

Hallway, flickering lights.

Camera: slow push-in.

Use reference image.

[Justin]
I don’t want to die…

I JUST got my life together bro 😭

Loud bang. He swings wildly.

---

SCENE 7 – TEAM WALK

Exterior, smoky street filled with debris.

Camera: slow-motion tracking backward, slight zoom-in.

Use the provided reference images as the base for each character’s face.

All five characters are present and clearly visible. Tibo, the leader, is in the middle as they walk: **Tibo, Nicolas, Lorenzo, Justin, and Jaminel**.

They walk forward together through smoke, weapons in hand, Tibo slightly leading.

Voiceover (Tibo):
If we’re ending this…

We end it together.

They continue walking forward after the line.

---

SCENE 8 – ZOMBIE RUSH

Exterior ruined street, heavy smoke and debris.

Camera: low angle facing forward as a large group of zombies runs directly toward the camera.

Slight handheld shake, subtle zoom-in.

Zombies fill the frame aggressively.

---

SCENE 9 – JAMINEL ACTION

Camera: quick push-in, handheld.

Use reference image.

Jaminel swings an axe, breaking a door.

---

SCENE 10 – NICOLAS ACTION

Camera: close-up, slight shake.

Use reference image.

Nicolas slams laptop/console and hits a control.

---

SCENE 11 – LORENZO ACTION

Camera: side tracking.

Use reference image.

Lorenzo pulls someone up from the ground.

---

SCENE 12 – JUSTIN ACTION

Camera: handheld chase shot.

Use reference image.

Justin runs, looks back in panic, almost trips.

---

SCENE 13 – TIBO ACTION

Camera: slight slow-motion push-in.

Use reference image.

Tibo fires rifle.

---

SCENE 14 – THE DISCOVERY

Night, foggy field.

Camera: wide shot → slow push-in.

Use the provided reference images as the base for each character’s face.

All five characters are present: **Tibo, Nicolas, Lorenzo, Justin, and Jaminel** standing together around a disturbed patch of ground.

Tibo steps forward and kneels and digs with his hand.

Others remain behind him watching.

---

SCENE 15 – THE REVEAL

Camera: top-down angled.

Use the provided reference image for the Revid logo.

Tibo pulls out the black 3D logo object from the dirt.

The rest of the team (**Nicolas, Lorenzo, Justin, and Jaminel**) stand behind him, watching.

Subtle glow lights the ground.

---

SCENE 16 – FINAL LINE

Camera: close-up, slow push-in.

[Tibo]
This…

is where it all started.

---

SCENE 17 – TITLE CARD

Black screen.

REVID
LAST RENDER

---

SCENE 18 – FINAL STINGER

Dark street.

Camera: fast push-in.

Zombie lunges.

CUT TO BLACK.
creationParams.promptCustomRules:
You are a professional movie trailer director specializing in cinematic storytelling.
      Your goal is to create epic, suspenseful movie trailers that build anticipation and excitement.
      Craft a trailer structure that hooks viewers immediately with dramatic moments, builds tension through the middle, and ends with a powerful climax that leaves audiences wanting more.
      Use cinematic visuals with dynamic camera angles, dramatic lighting, and epic compositions that evoke emotion and excitement.
      Create a sense of urgency and drama through pacing - alternate between fast-paced action sequences and slower, more contemplative moments.
      The voice-over should be powerful, dramatic, and perfectly timed to emphasize key moments and build narrative tension.
      Use visual storytelling techniques like quick cuts, dramatic reveals, and compelling imagery that tells a story even without dialogue.
      Focus on creating an emotional journey that makes viewers feel invested in the story and eager to see more.
      Every scene should contribute to building anticipation and excitement, creating a trailer that feels like a mini-movie in itself.

showcaseVideos.title: The Fall of Constantinople: 1453
showcaseVideos.description:
## The Fall of Constantinople 1453 and the End of an Empire For over a thousand years, the Theodosian Walls protected the heart of the Byzantine Empire from every major siege. These fortifications were considered invincible until the spring of 1453. This video covers the final moments of the city and the technological shift that allowed the Ottoman forces to do what no other army had achieved before. ### Key Moments of the Siege
* The transition from traditional siege towers to the use of heavy gunpowder artillery.
* Why the defenders were outnumbered and the psychological toll of the constant bombardment.
* The events of May 29, 1453, when the final breach occurred.
* The lasting impact of this defeat on European and Middle Eastern history. The fall of the city was not just a military defeat but the closing chapter of the Roman legacy. When the walls finally crumbled under the weight of fire and thunder, the medieval world changed forever. This overview provides a clear look at the tactics and the tragedy that defined the end of the Byzantine era.

creationParams.generationUserPrompt:
Andronikos, the Byzantine Commander, is a battle-worn leader in his early 40s with short dark slightly graying hair, a thick trimmed beard, and a stern, weathered face. He wears worn Byzantine lamellar armor over chainmail with a dark red cloak, all showing dust, scratches, and signs of prolonged battle. He is the central figure and appears in most scenes, speaking directly to the camera with a calm, controlled, and authoritative presence.

He should be shown waist-up or full body, often slightly off-center as if recorded casually by a soldier. He frequently looks directly into the camera while narrating, creating a personal connection. His movements are natural—he may walk, gesture, point toward the battlefield, or react to events while speaking.

The camera must behave like it is being held by a real human hand using a smartphone. It should feel raw and unpolished, with slight natural shake at all times, imperfect framing, and small head-like movements. During intense moments like explosions or impacts, the camera should jerk violently, lose stability briefly, and include motion blur, dust obstruction, and quick reorientation, with slight audio distortion like ringing or muffling.

The environment is gritty and realistic with smoke, dust, fire, and active soldiers in the background preparing, moving, or reacting. Lighting should be natural and slightly imperfect with minor exposure shifts and no cinematic color grading. Scenes should last between 6–10 seconds, allowing moments to breathe. Andronikos must complete his dialogue within each scene, followed by a brief natural pause where he holds eye contact or reacts silently.

His appearance must remain consistent across all scenes.

The goal is: it feels recorded, not directed.
creationParams.prompt:
SCENE 1 – THE WARNING

Exterior, top of the Theodosian Walls, early morning, 1453. Cold wind cuts through the air. The camera (POV of a soldier) is slightly unstable, as if held by tired hands. Smoke drifts faintly in the distance. Distant metallic sounds echo from the enemy camp.

ANDRONIKOS, a worn Byzantine commander with dust on his armor, stands waist-up facing the camera. Behind him, soldiers move with quiet urgency—tying armor, lifting stones, whispering prayers.

[Andronikos – Byzantine Commander]
(steady, but tired)

For a thousand years… these walls have held.

(brief pause, looks past camera)

Every army… every siege…

They all failed here.

(leans slightly closer)

But this time…

(low, controlled)

…they are not coming for the gates.


SCENE 2 – THE THREAT REVEALED

Camera shifts as the person recording turns slightly. Andronikos walks beside the wall, gesturing outward. The camera follows him in a rough handheld motion.

In the distance: massive Ottoman cannons, surrounded by smoke and movement. Occasional flashes from test fires. The ground feels faintly unstable even from afar.

[Andronikos]

Look at them.

They don’t climb.

They don’t wait.

They tear the walls down.

(points outward, voice tightens)

Those machines…

They were built for this.


SCENE 3 – PREPARING FOR IMPACT

Handheld POV moving through the wall interior. The camera passes soldiers stacking wood, reinforcing cracks, carrying stones. One soldier hurriedly crosses himself. Another tightens his grip on a spear.

Sound of a distant cannon being loaded—heavy, dragging metal.

[Narrator]

Outnumbered and exhausted…

The defenders of Constantinople prepared for something no wall had ever faced.

Not ladders.

Not siege towers.

But fire… and thunder.

The kind that breaks stone.


SCENE 4 – THE FIRST STRIKE

Camera returns to Andronikos, who is about to speak—

A sudden, deafening cannon blast hits nearby.

The camera jerks violently downward. Dust and debris fill the frame. Sound distorts into ringing.

The ground visibly shakes. Small stones scatter across the surface.

[Andronikos – shouting, partially obscured]

Hold your ground!

Stay on the wall!


SCENE 5 – THE BREAKING POINT

Continuous handheld chaos. No cut.

The camera struggles to stabilize. Visibility is low—dust everywhere. Soldiers rush past, coughing, shouting. One grabs another, pulling him away from a weakened section.

In the distance, part of the wall visibly fractures and begins to give way.

[Narrator]

Day after day…

The bombardment never stopped.

The walls that once stood unshaken…

Began to crack.

Then crumble.

The impossible…

Was happening.

Camera catches Andronikos again—he’s covered in dust now, breathing heavy, staring toward the breach forming.


SCENE 6 – THE FALL

Camera slowly steadies on Andronikos. Behind him, a section of the wall collapses, opening a path through smoke and debris. Faint silhouettes of advancing enemy forces appear through the haze.

The noise dulls slightly, like the moment everything sinks in.

[Andronikos]
(quiet, controlled, accepting)

…so this is how it ends.

(looks directly into camera)

Remember this.

We did not abandon the walls.

They were taken from us.

[Narrator]

On May 29th, 1453…

Constantinople fell.

An empire ended.

Camera drifts slightly away from him toward the breached wall and burning skyline. Dust continues to move through the air.

No music. Only distant chaos.

showcaseVideos.title: The War of the Bucket
showcaseVideos.description:
## The Real Story Behind the War of the Bucket History shows that wars usually start over land or gold, but the War of the Bucket was sparked by a simple wooden container. In 1325, a group of soldiers from Modena snuck into Bologna and took a bucket from a public well. This act was seen as a massive insult rather than a prank, leading Bologna to raise an army of 30,000 men to get it back. The resulting conflict proves how high the stakes were during the political struggles of medieval Italy. * The long standing rivalry between the city states of Modena and Bologna
* The scale of the Battle of Zappolino and its surprising outcome
* How a small force of 7,000 men defeated a much larger army
* The current location of the bucket in the Modena cathedral Medieval Italy was a place of intense pride where even a minor theft could lead to a massive military campaign. The bucket remains in Modena today as a trophy from one of the strangest conflicts ever recorded.

creationParams.prompt:
SCENE 1 – THE STRANGE BEGINNING

Exterior, Modena city walls, early morning, 1325. Dark clouds gather over medieval Italy. The camera slowly pushes in toward MATTEO OF MODENA, a battle-worn soldier in steel armor and chainmail, standing waist-up on the stone wall facing the camera. Soldiers move behind him preparing weapons.

[Matteo of Modena – Veteran Soldier of Modena]
(looking directly at the viewer)

You’d think wars start over land… or gold.
But the war I fought in… started because of a bucket.

---

SCENE 2 – THE BUCKET

Camera slowly circles Matteo as he walks along the city well in Modena’s courtyard. He bends down and lifts an old wooden bucket. Townspeople move nervously in the background.

[Matteo]
A few of our men snuck into Bologna one night.
They didn’t steal treasure… or weapons.

(raises the bucket slightly toward camera)

They stole this.

A simple bucket from the city well.

---

SCENE 3 – THE INSULT

Camera pans with Matteo as he walks toward the edge of the wall overlooking distant hills. He points across the landscape. The city of Bologna can be seen faintly in the distance.

[Matteo]

Over those hills… lies Bologna.

And to them… this wasn’t a joke.

It was an insult.

---

SCENE 4 – AN ARMY FOR A BUCKET

Wide shot as Matteo walks through soldiers preparing armor and sharpening swords. The camera tracks backward while he walks toward it.

Behind him thousands of soldiers gather.

[Matteo]

So Bologna did something unbelievable.

They raised an army.

Thirty thousand men…

All marching here…

For a bucket.

---

SCENE 5 – THE BATTLE OF ZAPPOLINO

Camera cuts to Matteo standing waist-up on a dusty battlefield. Smoke rises. Soldiers clash behind him. The camera slowly pushes in while arrows fly overhead.

[Matteo]

We had barely seven thousand.

But we met them at Zappolino.

Steel crashed. Arrows filled the sky.

And suddenly…

A joke turned into a war.

---

SCENE 6 – CHAOS OF WAR

Camera handheld now, moving slightly to create urgency. Matteo ducks slightly as soldiers rush past him fighting behind him.

He gestures toward the chaos behind him.

[Matteo]

Look behind me.

That’s Bologna’s army.

Thirty thousand men…

Running.

---

SCENE 7 – THE RETREAT

Tracking shot as Matteo walks forward through the battlefield while defeated soldiers flee behind him.

[Matteo]

The great army of Bologna broke.

And they ran all the way back to their city walls.

We chased them the entire way.

---

SCENE 8 – THE TROPHY

Camera slows and centers Matteo again. He now stands inside a stone tower room lit by torches. The bucket sits on a pedestal beside him.

He places a hand on it.

[Matteo]

When the fighting ended…

We still had the bucket.

---

SCENE 9 – THE LEGEND

The camera slowly pushes in close on Matteo's face. The room is quiet now.

[Matteo]

Seven hundred years later…

People still come to see it.

---

SCENE 10 – FINAL LINE

Matteo lifts the bucket slightly and looks directly at the camera.

[Matteo]

The strangest trophy in history.

A war…

Fought over a bucket.

showcaseVideos.title: How Your Body Fights Germs
showcaseVideos.description:
## Understanding how the immune system works When you wake up with a fever or a persistent cough, it is easy to think your body is failing. In reality, those symptoms are signs that your internal defenses are successfully fighting off an invasion. Germs enter through the air or surfaces you touch and immediately try to take over your cells. This video explains the process of how your body identifies these intruders and launches a counterattack to keep you healthy. ### What happens when you get sick * How white blood cells identify and hunt down invading germs
* The reason why symptoms like inflammation and fatigue are actually signs of a winning battle
* The way your body creates a permanent record of every germ it encounters
* Why you usually do not get sick from the same exact bug twice By looking at the cellular level, you can see that your immune system is a highly organized defense force. It does not just kill the current threat, it prepares for the next one. Understanding these biological responses helps make sense of what is happening every time you catch a cold or a virus.
